releases.summary: Intent compiler completion and the learning loop. assumption-ledger 1.0 (IC-004): every guess a project builds on has a person who can confirm it, an impact, an expiry and a way to be checked; one still open past its expiry fails the gate. change-proposal 1.0 (EV-006): each change to the AI configuration names its evidence and the eval cases it should decide, and can only be rolled out when a clean after-run passes with no regression. buaflow intake (IC-003) turns an issue-tracker export, a CSV or a plain list into draft intents that keep the original words and ask the missing questions. docs-lint warns on clarification questions that do not say which decision they change and on files over an eight-question budget (IC-002), and on acceptance criteria that are not EARS or that no design/tasks file traces (IC-005) — warnings in 3.x so no existing spec fails on upgrade. manual/ renders the same core workflow as plain playbooks for tools without slash commands, subagents, inline commands or hooks, and states which guarantees do not survive without session features (MT-007). /task gains a repair-loop budget by failure class (BC-007). reference-apps/matrix.json records which kinds of project the kit is proven on and prints the empty cells (EV-001).

Local clean-checkout CI (buaflow ci): clones HEAD into a temporary directory, runs commands.ciSetup (with {source} for untracked files such as .env that a hosted runner would get from secrets) and the checkout's own gate, and records docs/evidence/ci-run.json with provider local-clean-checkout. assess counts a successful local run as evidence for the ci control, so ciMode local-only is no longer a permanent R2 blocker. check-config no longer fails inside CI (CI=true or a buaflow ci run) for a pre-push hook under .git/hooks, which no checkout can ever contain. Phase A.5 now says to keep rules in step with protected paths, which each project decides. No artifact schema changed.

Onboarding (EV-008): QUICKSTART.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md written from the findings of the first outside trial (K-1..K-14 and its eval baseline), and a worked sample on a reference app with real output. npm run check now fails when an onboarding document names a buaflow command, flag, script or link that does not exist. buaflow assess and buaflow benchmark print their per-control table in human mode; their JSON output is unchanged.

Production-Qualified App benchmark (EV-002): buaflow benchmark scores functional, engineering and operations from the readiness manifest, the independent verifier, the repository probe, the EP-002..007 validators and eval runs, with no number typed by anyone and no per-app branching; a claim is worth full marks only with independently confirmed evidence, manual-only evidence scores zero, and a missing artifact scores zero for every project alike. Also from the EV-009 eval baseline: check-config warns when permissions.allow names a package manager the project has no lockfile for, and check-config, docs-lint and board.js now resolve a relative root so a project stack.json is no longer silently ignored when the root is given as ".". No artifact schema changed.

Fixes from the first trial on a project the kit did not write (EV-009, tracked as EV-010). New command buaflow assess answers which readiness level a project is at from probes of the repository itself, with no manifest and before anything is installed; a control is pass only when a probe is conclusive or a command really ran, and never not-applicable. doctor reports whether the root is inside a git work tree and whether it is the git root. check-config tells a brownfield CLAUDE.md to prepend @AGENTS.md instead of reading as an order to rewrite it. The default components/ui protection no longer recommends re-running the shadcn CLI over existing files, and guard-bash blocks shadcn add --overwrite. The gate re-runs a failed verify once: failing twice is reproducible; failing then passing is recorded as flaky in .verify-flakes.jsonl and does not block in adoption mode (it still fails in production mode). readiness.js rejects a manifest whose generatedAt is more than five minutes in the future, which was never valid input. No artifact schema changed.

Reproducible eval harness (EV-004). Two new public artifacts, eval-case 1.0 and eval-run 1.0, replace the Markdown eval format whose results table was filled in by hand and could not say which revision of a case it had judged. A run pins caseRevision, so editing a case's prompt, criteria or pass threshold turns every run that claimed to pass it stale instead of leaving a passing record standing; renaming or retiring a case does not, because neither changes what the case asks. The outcome is re-derived from the per-criterion verdicts on every read, a run graded by the case's own author is refused, and a run recorded as continuing an earlier session cannot pass. Across runs the harness reports what a single run cannot show: an ablation round that did not change the outcome (the file under test is not what produces the behaviour) and the same case, commit and model disagreeing with itself. Additive: a project with no docs/evals/*.json is not checked. The four Markdown starter cases are gone; their content survives in claude-setup/evals/EV-00x.json.

Profile-driven budgets (EP-007): application-profile gains an optional budgets field at schema 1.1, and a new public artifact, budget-evidence 1.0, records what an app measured without recording what it is allowed to be. The ceiling lives in the profile, so the same app passes or fails depending on what it claims to be. Measured numbers are re-derived from the cited evidence files, and a budgeted metric nothing measures fails. Additive: 1.0 profiles stay readable and simply declare no budgets, and a project without docs/evidence/budgets.json is not checked.

Operational readiness (EP-005): a new public artifact, operational-readiness 1.0, plus .claude/operational-readiness.js. A backup procedure must cite a rehearsal that really destroyed and restored the database with identical data, and incident hooks become a contract — each with a signal precise enough to alert on, a detector whose files exist, a severity, an owner, and a runbook anchor the validator resolves against the real headings. Where a security baseline exists, every trust boundary it declares must be watched by a hook. Additive: a project without docs/evidence/operational-readiness.json is not checked.

Supply-chain evidence (EP-004): a new public artifact, supply-chain 1.0, plus .claude/supply-chain.js. The licence summary is re-derived from the project's own SBOMs on every run so it cannot be written optimistically, SBOMs and published artifacts are pinned by a sha256 the validator recomputes, an unreviewed licence fails, and build provenance must agree with evidence/ci-run.json and with the revision the readiness manifest graded. Additive: a project without docs/evidence/supply-chain.json is not checked.

Security baseline with threat boundaries and a real external control set (EP-003): a new public artifact, security-baseline 1.0, plus .claude/security-baseline.js and a pinned copy of OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 level 1 in standards/control-sets/. Every control of the named set must be answered, a control that cannot be cited as met must point at an approved exception in requirement-coverage.json, and threat boundaries become data a reviewer can check rather than a paragraph. Additive: a project without docs/evidence/security-baseline.json is not checked.

Requirement coverage with approved exceptions (EP-002): a new public artifact, requirement-coverage 1.0, plus .claude/coverage.js. A requirement may be accepted without proof only through an exception carrying an owner, a reason, a risk and an expiry date, and an expired exception fails the gate. Additive: a project without docs/evidence/requirement-coverage.json is not checked and behaves exactly as before, which is why this is minor rather than major.

Pack contract v2 (PP-010): a pack is a recipe plus assertions, not a template. An adopter with .claude/packs/*.json must rewrite them by hand — the migration is registered manual because v1 recorded no setup commands to derive a recipe from. Also adds the independent verifier (BC-006, .claude/verifier.js and buaflow audit), the evidence-freshness control (EP-010), and the failure taxonomy (EV-003).
Last release before the kit had a stated release policy. Recorded here so the matrix has a before state to compare against, not because 2.x releases were versioned under this policy.

deprecations.migration: Manual: v1 recorded no setup commands, so no deterministic transform exists. Rewrite each .claude/packs/*.json against schemas/pack.schema.json; templates/pack.tpl.json and packs/ are worked examples. See D-011.
deprecations.note: Announced and removed in the same release, with no notice period. This is recorded honestly rather than backdated: the kit had no release policy when the change was made, which is the gap EV-007 closes. Under the policy now in force this would have required a minor release announcing the deprecation first, and it is the last change permitted to skip that.
